prompt: A route planner accepts any Route implementation through one read-only contract: every route returns the same ordered stops and travel-time units, and no route adds required inputs. A regional route subtype changes how travel times are computed but preserves those results and invariants for every caller. How should the regional route type relate to Route?

options.text: RegionalRoute may implement Route.
Keep RegionalRoute as an unrelated collaborator that every caller must special-case.
Subclass Route but require regional callers to provide a new mandatory territory argument.
Copy Route’s stop list into a new type and let callers choose between two unrelated APIs.

feedback.reason: Every route receives the same inputs and returns the same promised result shape.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A subtype must be usable wherever the base type is expected without changing the caller-visible behavior.
details.scenarioApplication: RegionalRoute changes its calculation but still returns the same stop and time contract to every planner.
details.errorCorrection: Implementation variation alone does not require a separate collaborator when the object remains a valid Route for all clients.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a regional route needed extra caller input or changed what a returned duration meant, keep that behavior behind a separate collaborator or API.
details.transfer: Test substitutability at the public contract: required inputs, promised outputs, and preserved invariants.

messages.text: The prompt states that callers consume the same Route contract and the regional type is behaviorally interchangeable.
A new required argument is a stronger precondition and breaks callers that only know Route.
Duplicating the API discards the common substitutable contract the case already provides.

prompt: An invoice service can calculate either a standard or negotiated tax amount. The invoice remains the same domain object, and an authorized account setting chooses the tax calculator for each calculation; callers still use the same invoice API. Where should the two calculation behaviors live?

options.text: Use an account-selected TaxCalculator collaborator.
Make NegotiatedInvoice a subtype and move the selected calculation rule into invoice identity.
Create one Invoice subtype per tax rule and require callers to select a concrete invoice class.
Let each Invoice caller calculate tax independently before calling the invoice.

feedback.reason: Tax behavior changes per calculation while Invoice identity and caller contract remain fixed.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Composition keeps an independently selected behavior alongside a stable domain object.
details.scenarioApplication: Invoice stays the same object while the account’s chosen TaxCalculator supplies one calculation.
details.errorCorrection: Do not turn a policy choice into a subtype hierarchy when the same invoice can use the selected calculator without changing its identity or contract.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If negotiated invoices were distinct domain types with different caller-visible guarantees, a subtype could be appropriate.
details.transfer: Ask whether the variation changes the object’s substitutable kind or is a behavior the same object uses.

messages.text: The tax behavior is selected independently per calculation and does not change what kind of invoice the object is.
Tax selection is a collaborator variation, not an invoice-kind distinction in the prompt.
Duplicating the invariant across callers makes the same invoice contract depend on caller implementation.

prompt: A public DocumentReader promises that callers can request text for any published document. A proposed EncryptedReader requires callers to supply a decryption key that ordinary DocumentReader callers do not have; without it, the reader cannot return the promised text. Can EncryptedReader safely be modeled as a DocumentReader subtype?

options.text: Keep key-dependent reading behind a separate reader API.
Yes; a subtype may require extra caller input whenever its implementation is more secure.
Yes; inherit DocumentReader and return an empty string when no key is supplied.
Make DocumentReader require a key for every document, including unencrypted ones.

feedback.reason: Ordinary DocumentReader callers lack the new required key.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A subtype cannot strengthen the conditions a base-type caller must meet to get the base promise.
details.scenarioApplication: EncryptedReader needs information its callers do not possess under the DocumentReader contract.
details.errorCorrection: Security requirements may justify a distinct API or injected key provider, but do not make the subtype valid by changing the expected caller behavior.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the key were supplied through the same existing reader contract and every caller could still obtain the promised document text, the implementation could be substitutable.
details.transfer: Compare the candidate’s required inputs with what a base-typed caller is allowed to provide.

messages.text: A caller holding only a DocumentReader cannot satisfy the added key requirement, so the candidate is not substitutable.
Returning empty text weakens the promised result for ordinary callers.
Changing the base contract imposes a new requirement on every existing reader client.

prompt: A timetable API accepts any Schedule and promises that `eventsFor(day)` returns every event for that day, including canceled events marked with their status. A proposed ArchivedSchedule silently omits canceled events because it is optimized for public display. What is the sound model for the public-only view?

options.text: Use a public-only Schedule projection.
Subclass Schedule and hide canceled events from the inherited method.
Subclass Schedule and return an empty list for canceled days.
Change every Schedule caller to know whether it received the archived subtype.

feedback.reason: The base schedule promises canceled events that this view omits.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A specialized view with a narrower result is not a behavioral subtype of the complete schedule contract.
details.scenarioApplication: The public-only projection may be useful, but consumers that need all events must continue to receive Schedule behavior.
details.errorCorrection: Do not treat a display filter as a subtype if it violates the base type’s completeness promise.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the base type promised only currently visible events, the archived view could satisfy that contract.
details.transfer: A subtype must preserve the base type’s postconditions, not merely share its name or data structure.

messages.text: Omitting canceled events weakens the base result guarantee.
An empty list falsely says no events exist when the base contract includes canceled ones.
Requiring subtype checks changes the behavior expected from a Schedule value.

prompt: A media pipeline accepts any Encoder through the same `encode(source, format)` contract. The new LosslessEncoder accepts the same inputs, returns a decodable file with the same format metadata, and never discards source samples; callers do not need to know which encoder instance they receive. Which relation best represents LosslessEncoder?

options.text: LosslessEncoder may implement Encoder.
Make LosslessEncoder an unrelated helper that every pipeline stage must detect by concrete type.
Subclass Encoder but make the caller provide a lossless-only quality flag.
Use LosslessEncoder as a wrapper that silently changes the requested output format.

feedback.reason: The encoder strengthens an output guarantee without adding caller obligations.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Subtype variation is appropriate when an implementation changes internal behavior while preserving the public contract.
details.scenarioApplication: LosslessEncoder receives the same arguments and returns the same promised kind of decodable output, with the additional no-sample-loss guarantee.
details.errorCorrection: A stronger guarantee is compatible with substitutability; a stronger caller requirement or weaker result would not be.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a codec required extra source metadata absent from the base API, that codec should be a separate collaborator or adapter.
details.transfer: Check both directions: extra guarantees may refine a subtype, but extra caller obligations usually break substitutability.

messages.text: The same inputs, outputs, and invariants hold for every encoder implementation in this pipeline.
A lossless-only required flag strengthens the precondition and breaks existing Encoder callers.
Changing the requested format violates the output contract rather than specializing behavior safely.

prompt: A delivery label can be rendered in either a thermal-printer layout or a PDF layout. The Shipment object stays the same, and the chosen renderer is selected per destination; both renderers consume a ShipmentSnapshot and produce an artifact through the same output contract. How should the two renderings be modeled?

options.text: Use a destination-selected LabelRenderer with Shipment.
Create ThermalShipment and PdfShipment subtypes even though layout is selected per destination.
Put printer-specific formatting branches in every caller that requests a label.
Make a PDF subtype of ThermalLabel because both represent printed labels.

feedback.reason: Destination changes presentation, not the shipment’s domain type.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A collaborator represents a behavior selected alongside a stable domain object.
details.scenarioApplication: Each destination chooses a renderer for the same shipment snapshot; Shipment identity and caller contract do not change.
details.errorCorrection: Do not encode an output-format choice in the Shipment subtype when format varies per rendering request.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the domain distinguished shipments with different non-interchangeable fulfillment guarantees, subtype modeling might be warranted for that separate distinction.
details.transfer: Place behavior that varies independently of an entity in a collaborator rather than multiplying entity subtypes.

messages.text: The variation is an independently selected rendering behavior, not a different kind of Shipment.
Duplicating formatting policy across callers makes the same output contract caller-dependent.
A PDF artifact is not a specialized thermal label and does not substitute for it.

prompt: Every InspectionReport exposes a `condition()` operation that returns one of the allowed inspection categories. A proposed CertifiedReport adds a signature but keeps the same category set and operation behavior; any client that accepts InspectionReport can read it unchanged. How should CertifiedReport relate to InspectionReport?

options.text: CertifiedReport may extend InspectionReport.
Keep it as an unrelated collaborator because adding a signature always changes the report contract.
Subclass it but remove `condition()` because certified reports use the signature instead.
Make every report caller check for CertifiedReport before reading the category.

feedback.reason: The signature is additive and leaves every report operation available.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A subtype may add behavior while preserving the base type’s observable guarantees.
details.scenarioApplication: CertifiedReport still returns the same condition category; its signature is extra information rather than a replacement behavior.
details.errorCorrection: Do not confuse an added capability with a changed contract; the key test is whether base clients still work.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If certification changed category meaning or removed the operation for some reports, the type would need a distinct contract.
details.transfer: Subtypes can refine guarantees, but they must retain every behavior their base clients rely on.

messages.text: An additional guarantee does not prevent the certified report from honoring the existing base operation.
Removing a promised operation violates the base contract.
No caller distinction is required when the subtype supports the same operation and result contract.

prompt: A reservation object remains the same domain record whether a user chooses standard or accessible room matching. The matcher is chosen per search request, and both matchers return candidate room IDs under the same result contract; neither matcher represents a reservation. Where should the matching variation live?

options.text: Select RoomMatcher per search, outside Reservation identity.
Create StandardReservation and AccessibleReservation even though one reservation can be searched under either matcher.
Make RoomMatcher a subtype of Reservation because it affects candidate rooms.
Copy the matching algorithm into each caller so each screen can choose its own rule.

feedback.reason: Matcher choice varies by request, not by Reservation kind.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A collaborator can vary per operation while the domain object keeps one identity and stable contract.
details.scenarioApplication: The request selects a matcher; the resulting candidate IDs follow the same contract without changing Reservation.
details.errorCorrection: Do not turn the algorithm that processes a reservation into a subtype of the reservation itself.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If reservations themselves represented distinct products with different lifecycle or caller-visible guarantees, a subtype could be considered separately.
details.transfer: Ask whether the candidate is a kind of the entity or an independent behavior applied to it.

messages.text: A single reservation may be evaluated by different matchers, so the variation is not an entity kind.
A matcher is a behavior service, not a reservation with the reservation contract.
Duplicating the algorithm across screens risks inconsistent results and is not required by the scenario.

prompt: A `Route` base contract guarantees that every route accepts a pair of valid endpoints and returns a connected path or a documented no-path result. A proposed ScenicRoute additionally requires a minimum number of waypoints before it will search. Should ScenicRoute be a Route subtype?

options.text: Expose ScenicRoute through a separate policy or API.
Yes; subclasses may require more input as long as their names communicate the restriction.
Yes; return no-path whenever too few waypoints are supplied, even when a path exists.
Make Route require waypoints for every route, including routes with no scenic constraint.

feedback.reason: The subtype rejects valid base inputs unless callers supply extra waypoints.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Behavioral substitutability requires the subtype to accept every input the base contract accepts.
details.scenarioApplication: ScenicRoute needs an extra input that ordinary Route callers are not required to provide.
details.errorCorrection: A descriptive subtype name does not repair a contract violation; callers typed as Route must not fail unexpectedly.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the waypoint rule were an optional parameter in the existing base API, ScenicRoute could preserve the contract while adding a mode.
details.transfer: Compare accepted inputs before treating a specialized behavior as a subtype.

messages.text: A base-typed caller can provide valid endpoints without waypoints, so the subtype strengthens a precondition.
Returning no-path when a valid path exists weakens the base result promise.
Changing the base type imposes a requirement absent from the current contract.

prompt: An exhibit uses one maintenance policy chosen by the building operator. The exhibit remains the same object when policy changes, and the policy can be reused by many exhibits; policy selection does not change any Exhibit caller contract. How should the policy choice be represented?

options.text: Reference a replaceable MaintenancePolicy from Exhibit.
Create one Exhibit subtype for every maintenance policy and encode policy choice in its type.
Make MaintenancePolicy a subtype of Exhibit because it controls exhibit commands.
Copy the policy rules into each caller so the Exhibit has no policy association.

feedback.reason: Policy selection changes without changing Exhibit identity or API.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Composition models a has-a behavior dependency while the owner object keeps its identity.
details.scenarioApplication: Exhibit continues to be an Exhibit; the operator-selected policy changes which commands are allowed.
details.errorCorrection: Do not create concrete entity subclasses for a setting that can vary independently and be shared.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If policy variants defined enduring kinds of exhibits with distinct external guarantees, a subtype could represent that stable distinction.
details.transfer: Keep independently configured behavior as a collaborator unless it changes the object’s substitutable kind.

messages.text: A reusable, independently selected rule is not a distinct kind of Exhibit.
The policy supplies behavior but does not have the Exhibit’s identity or caller contract.
Copying rules into callers fragments the single policy that the scenario says is reused.

prompt: A payout processor accepts any Processor and promises that a settled payout is either recorded once or returns a retryable failure with the same payout key. A proposed RegionalProcessor follows the same input rules and result contract while adding regional routing internally. Can RegionalProcessor be treated as a Processor subtype?

options.text: RegionalProcessor may implement Processor.
No; regional routing must always be a collaborator even when callers use one unchanged processor contract.
Yes, but it may return success before recording the payout because regional routing is asynchronous.
Yes, but require a region code that existing Processor callers do not provide.

feedback.reason: Regional routing preserves the processor’s idempotent result contract.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A subtype can replace the base implementation if the same caller-visible guarantees remain true.
details.scenarioApplication: RegionalProcessor preserves the exactly-once record-or-retryable-failure contract while selecting a route internally.
details.errorCorrection: Implementation structure does not decide substitutability; the accepted inputs and outcomes do.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If regional routing exposed different failure or duplicate behavior, represent that variant behind a separate contract or collaborator.
details.transfer: Compare the observable behavior from the base caller’s perspective before accepting an implementation as a subtype.

messages.text: The routing variation is internal and does not change the public preconditions or outcome guarantee.
Success before the payout is recorded violates the stated Processor result contract.
The added region argument strengthens the caller precondition.

prompt: A document signer can use either an in-house signing service or an external provider. The signer object remains the same request, and the provider is selected for each delivery attempt; provider credentials and availability are managed separately. How should the provider variation relate to SignRequest?

options.text: Use a selected SigningProvider with SignRequest.
Create an ExternalSignRequest subtype whose identity changes whenever a provider is selected.
Make SigningProvider a subtype of SignRequest because both participate in signing.
Have each SignRequest caller own credentials and decide which provider protocol to call.

feedback.reason: Provider choice changes independently for each delivery attempt.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A collaborator represents an independently selected participant with its own responsibility and lifecycle.
details.scenarioApplication: The same SignRequest can be delivered through either provider, and the provider owns its credentials and availability behavior.
details.errorCorrection: Do not confuse the object being acted on with the service that performs the action.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If provider-specific requests had different domain guarantees and were never switched per request, a separate request subtype might be worth evaluating.
details.transfer: Model distinct roles as collaborators when one object invokes another responsibility rather than becoming that responsibility.

messages.text: Provider choice changes the delivery mechanism, not the request’s domain identity.
A provider does not expose the SignRequest object’s caller contract; it performs a distinct role.
Credentials and protocol handling are explicitly managed separately from callers.

prompt: A read-only view implements the same query-only `Profile` contract used by account screens: callers request display fields, no operation mutates a Profile, and the documented unavailable-field result is preserved. It adds a provenance badge but keeps every existing caller operation intact. Should ReadOnlyProfile be a subtype of Profile?

options.text: ReadOnlyProfile may implement Profile.
No; any added presentation field requires a separate unrelated type.
Yes, but remove the unavailable-field result because a read-only view has no missing data.
Make every account screen test for ReadOnlyProfile before calling Profile operations.

feedback.reason: The read-only variant preserves the base fields and unavailable result.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A subtype may offer additional information while preserving the base set of observable operations.
details.scenarioApplication: ReadOnlyProfile retains the same fields and unavailable behavior; its provenance badge is an additive capability.
details.errorCorrection: Read-only is not automatically incompatible with Profile; the deciding issue is whether the base contract requires updates.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If Profile’s contract included a required update operation, this read-only view could not substitute without a valid update behavior.
details.transfer: Check the full base API, not just whether the subtype adds or omits a feature in its name.

messages.text: The added field does not alter the base contract, so ordinary Profile clients can still use the view.
Removing a documented result changes behavior expected by existing callers.
A type check is unnecessary when the subtype supports all base operations.

prompt: A campaign character has a permanent `claimReward` operation with a contract that rejects ineligible claims and never changes quest completion. A proposed AutoCompletingCharacter makes the call succeed by completing the quest first, a side effect the base contract forbids. Can AutoCompletingCharacter replace Character?

options.text: Keep quest completion outside Character’s reward operation.
Yes; completing the quest is a helpful specialization of reward claiming.
Yes; override the base operation and report success after the extra quest change.
Change Character’s contract so reward claiming always completes an eligible quest first.

feedback.reason: The proposed subtype adds a state change forbidden by the base operation.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Substitutability covers side effects and invariants, not only return values.
details.scenarioApplication: The subtype adds a quest mutation to a call that must remain read-only with respect to quest completion.
details.errorCorrection: A convenient extra action is still a contract change when callers rely on the base operation not performing it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the use case explicitly requested an atomic “complete quest and claim reward” operation, it should be a separate command with that contract.
details.transfer: Compare state changes as well as method signatures when reviewing a subtype.

messages.text: The base contract explicitly forbids changing quest completion during reward claim.
Reporting success after an unrequested state change violates the promised side-effect boundary.
Changing the base contract would alter all existing Character callers.

prompt: A cold-chain shipment can be assigned to a Carrier only after the carrier acknowledges custody and meets the temperature band. Carrier selection changes per shipment, while Shipment keeps the same fields and lifecycle. Where should the carrier-specific assignment behavior live?

options.text: Select Carrier through Shipment assignment, not subtype identity.
Create one Shipment subtype for each carrier so its custody acknowledgement becomes part of shipment type.
Make Carrier a subtype of Shipment because both participate in delivery.
Let dispatch callers bypass the custody check whenever a carrier is familiar.

feedback.reason: Carrier selection changes across shipments while Shipment remains the same kind.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An association or collaborator models the selected carrier while Shipment remains the stable domain record.
details.scenarioApplication: The shipment refers to whichever carrier passes the same stated band and acknowledgement conditions.
details.errorCorrection: Do not encode a changing assignment value as a permanent subtype of the assigned entity.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If shipment categories had permanently different guarantees and different callers, subtype modeling could express that separate domain distinction.
details.transfer: Assignments that change over an object’s lifetime usually belong in relationships or collaborators, not in the object’s class identity.

messages.text: Carrier choice varies independently for the same shipment; it is not a distinct shipment kind.
A carrier has its own identity and does not satisfy the Shipment contract.
The stated assignment precondition applies regardless of caller familiarity.

prompt: A campaign reward evaluator is selected by the campaign’s ruleset. The Character remains the same object while the campaign revision changes; evaluator implementations receive the same read-only inputs and return the same eligibility result shape. How should reward evaluation vary across campaign revisions?

options.text: Select RewardEvaluator by campaign revision.
Create a Character subtype for every campaign revision even though the same character moves between revisions.
Make RewardEvaluator a subtype of Character because it reads character state.
Duplicate reward calculations in the UI and persistence callers.

feedback.reason: Campaign revision selects the rule implementation; Character remains unchanged.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A decision strategy chosen by external context is a collaborator, while the subject of the decision retains its own lifecycle.
details.scenarioApplication: The campaign selects the evaluator for its revision, and the same Character is evaluated under that rule.
details.errorCorrection: Do not make the entity’s class represent every external rule context that can be applied to it.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If campaign-specific characters had distinct enduring behavior contracts independent of evaluator choice, subtypes might be useful.
details.transfer: Keep policy selection near the operation that chooses it, rather than multiplying entity subtypes for contextual rules.

messages.text: Campaign revision changes do not change the character’s domain kind or identity.
An evaluator performs a decision service and does not satisfy Character’s entity contract.
Duplicating the same rule across callers can produce different eligibility results.

prompt: Every Match implementation accepts the same two team IDs and returns one of the documented legal-state outcomes. A proposed ExhibitionMatch subtype additionally allows a completed match to be forfeited, an operation the base Match contract rejects. Can ExhibitionMatch safely substitute for Match?

options.text: Keep ExhibitionMatch outside Match’s rejecting contract.
Yes; accepting more operations is always safe even when it changes a documented rejection.
Yes; override the rejection only for callers that know the concrete subtype.
Make every Match caller detect ExhibitionMatch before submitting a forfeit.

feedback.reason: Base callers rely on completed matches rejecting a forfeit.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A subtype must preserve the base type’s state-transition and rejection guarantees.
details.scenarioApplication: ExhibitionMatch would permit a completed-match transition that every Match caller expects to be rejected.
details.errorCorrection: “More permissive” behavior can still violate a contract when the base guarantees a specific rejection outcome.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the base contract allowed completed-match corrections under explicit authority, a specialized implementation could preserve that same authorization rule.
details.transfer: Review both allowed transitions and required rejections when assessing substitutability.

messages.text: Callers rely on completed matches rejecting a forfeit; changing that outcome violates the base contract.
The base-type guarantee cannot depend on which caller remembers a subtype check.
Subtype checks make behavior differ for a caller that only knows Match.

prompt: A marketplace listing may render through a compact card or a full detail page. The same Listing object supplies the same underlying fields, and a view adapter chooses which presentation is produced for the current screen. How should the presentation variation be modeled?

options.text: Use a view adapter for Listing presentation.
Create CompactListing and FullListing subtypes and change the listing’s identity when the screen changes.
Make the view adapter a subtype of Listing because it reads listing data.
Put separate formatting and field-selection rules in every screen caller.

feedback.reason: Screen choice selects a representation, not a new Listing kind.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A composition boundary separates domain identity from a behavior selected by a consumer.
details.scenarioApplication: The adapter consumes the same Listing fields and renders one chosen view without changing the Listing object.
details.errorCorrection: Do not model UI representation as domain inheritance when the domain object has not changed.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If listing categories carried different permanent business guarantees, those categories could be modeled separately from view format.
details.transfer: Keep representation choices outside entity identity when clients vary presentation independently.

messages.text: Screen choice is a presentation variation and does not create a new kind of Listing.
An adapter produces a view; it does not satisfy the Listing entity contract.
Duplicating view logic across callers fragments a single presentation decision.
